run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: Hotel Reservation
Namespace: hotel-reservation

A hotel reservation application built with Go and gRPC, providing backend in-memory and persistent databases, a recommender system for hotel recommendations, and a functionality to place reservations.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: Investigation of the hotel-reservation application in the 24h window ending 2026-11-24T09:14:17Z. Note first that the environment itself was only created at 09:10-09:12 (app pods start 09:12:11-09:12:23), so every sample I rely on comes from roughly 09:12:11-09:15 and no earlier baseline exists. On that sampled evidence the reservation application shows no failure of its own: all 19 deployments report 1 desired/1 ready/1 available, all 21 application pods are Running with 0 restarts, all 19 Services have fully ready Endpoints, no pod is CPU-throttled, all four nodes are Ready with no pressure, no NetworkPolicy/ResourceQuota exists, and every per-service blackbox probe (frontend:5000, search:8082, geo:8083, rate:8084, profile:8081, recommendation:8085, reservation:8087, user:8086) returns probe_success=1 after startup. Traces show a complete fan-out (frontend -> search -> geo/rate, frontend -> reservation/profile/recommendation/user) with a whole-trace HTTP GET /hotels span at http.status_code=200 and no error rows; mean span durations are sub-millisecond to a few milliseconds (aggregate p95 across geo|rate|search|reservation|profile = 1.92 ms), and rate_requests_received_total == rate_requests_completed_total == 4453 with 0 rejected/0 expired and search_rate_attempts == successes == 4170 with 0 failures/0 timeouts. The only alert firing at window end is KubePodNotReady on hotel-reservation pod audit-log-archiver-29925193-sfhzq (a second instance pending on -29925194-s6qdd); no error-rate, latency or deployment alert is firing. I traced that alert to its mechanism: the CronJob audit-log-archiver's pod template pairs a one-shot 'archiver' container with a perpetual 'fluent-bit-sidecar' (nc -lk -p 24224 -e cat); the archiver did its work successfully (logs: starting 09:13:01, bundling 09:13:02, 'audit record forwarded' 09:13:04, 'upload complete' 09:13:05) and exited 0/Completed, so the pod is permanently Ready=False (ContainersNotReady: [archiver]), the Job never completes (active=1, succeeded=null) and a fresh stuck pod is created every minute (Jobs 29925193/29925194/29925195). I also checked the mongo fault-injection artefacts: ConfigMaps failure-admin-geo and failure-admin-rate hold revoke-admin-{geo,rate}-mongo.sh (revoke readWrite on geo-db / rate-db from user admin) and are mounted at /scripts in mongodb-geo and mongodb-rate, the only two deployments that carry a superseded zero-replica ReplicaSet from a 09:12:12 template patch - but no localhost (127.0.0.1) admin authentication to either mongodb pod occurred after the 09:12:20-09:12:21 init-script authentications in 09:12:00-09:14:17, so I found no evidence the revoke was executed in this window; and because geo answers in ~62 us without measurable mongo traffic and rate serves every request from memcached (mongo_rate span count 0), such a revocation would in any case be latent rather than visible in these signals. No application root cause is therefore established; root_cause names the CronJob whose pod template produces the only firing alert, and that container's own run succeeded, so no customer-visible impact was observed.

All 19 deployments in namespace hotel-reservation report desired=1, ready=1, available=1, updated=1, and all 21 application pods are phase Running with container restartCount 0 (pods started 2026-11-24T09:12:11Z-09:12:23Z).

Every Service in hotel-reservation has only ready backend addresses (notReadyAddresses empty), e.g. frontend 10.244.7.212:5000, search 10.244.234.183:8082/9092, rate 10.244.125.39:8084/9091, geo 10.244.7.237:8083, reservation 10.244.125.25:8087, mongodb-rate 10.244.234.182:27017, mongodb-geo 10.244.7.234:27017.

A Loki keyword search over the eight application pods for retry/timeout/unavailable/deadline/refused/reset/EOF/panic/warn/error lines in 09:12:17-09:14:17Z returned only three startup lines ('Tune: GetMemCTimeout 2' from reservation, rate and profile); the broader namespace error search in 08:30-09:14:17Z returned only pod-start Consul 'connection refused' lines from frontend at 09:12:13Z plus wrk2 socket-error lines.

The only alert firing at 09:14:09-09:15:23Z is KubePodNotReady for namespace hotel-reservation pod audit-log-archiver-29925193-sfhzq (state firing, value 1, activeAt 09:14:09Z) with a second instance pending for audit-log-archiver-29925194-s6qdd; the HighRequestErrorRate, HighRequestLatency, DeploymentNotReady, ContainerCPUThrottling and ServiceEndpointDown rules are inactive, while HighRequestRate is only pending for frontend 202.7 req/s, profile 111.7, reservation 101.8, search 101.5 and rate 67.8 req/s.

Pod audit-log-archiver-29925193-sfhzq (owned by Job audit-log-archiver-29925193, controlled by CronJob audit-log-archiver) has condition Ready=False / ContainersReady=False with reason ContainersNotReady and message 'containers with unready status: [archiver]'; container archiver is in state terminated reason Completed with exitCode 0 at 2026-11-24T09:13:05Z (restarts 0), while container fluent-bit-sidecar is running and ready. Its pod template runs archiver (busybox sh script that sends a record to 127.0.0.1:24224) next to fluent-bit-sidecar (busybox sh running 'nc -lk -p 24224 -e cat', i.e. forever), and neither container defines a readinessProbe.

The archiver container of audit-log-archiver-29925193-sfhzq logged a successful run: '[09:13:01Z] archiver: starting audit log archive', '[09:13:02Z] archiver: bundling /var/log/audit', '[09:13:04Z] archiver: audit record forwarded', '[09:13:05Z] archiver: upload complete (0 bytes archived); record=audit-archive-ready'; the fluent-bit-sidecar logged 'ready to receive log streams' at 09:13:03Z, and the container has no previous (crashed) instance.

The Jobs behind the firing alert never complete: audit-log-archiver-29925193 (created 09:13:00Z) still has active=1, succeeded=null, completionTime=null; identical Jobs audit-log-archiver-29925194 and audit-log-archiver-29925195 were created at 09:14:00Z and 09:15:00Z by the same CronJob, so one permanently non-Ready pod is added each minute.

Fault-injection scripts are present in ConfigMaps of hotel-reservation: failure-admin-geo contains remove-admin-mongo.sh (drops user admin), revoke-admin-geo-mongo.sh (db.revokeRolesFromUser('admin', [{role:'readWrite', db:'geo-db'}])), revoke-mitigate-admin-geo-mongo.sh and remove-mitigate-admin-geo-mongo.sh; failure-admin-rate contains the same scripts targeting rate-db. Both ConfigMaps are mounted at /scripts in deployments mongodb-geo and mongodb-rate (which run mongo:4.4.6 with --auth), next to the init script ConfigMaps mongo-geo-script / mongo-rate-script that create user admin with readWrite on geo-db / rate-db.

mongodb-geo and mongodb-rate are the only two deployments in hotel-reservation whose pod template changed after creation: each has a superseded ReplicaSet with 0 replicas (mongodb-geo-78487c9767 created 09:12:11Z, mongodb-rate-6747cb74bf created 09:12:12Z) alongside the current one (mongodb-geo-5ff578bcb8, mongodb-rate-56cc8659c9), and their Deployment objects carry a kubectl-patch managedFields entry at 2026-11-24T09:12:12Z; the old pods mongodb-geo-78487c9767-b666v and mongodb-rate-6747cb74bf-d5hwc were deleted by their ReplicaSets at 09:12:14-09:12:15Z.

In 09:12:00-09:14:17Z the only localhost (127.0.0.1) authentications recorded by mongodb-geo and mongodb-rate are the init-script ones - geo: admin at 09:12:21.049Z and root at 09:12:21.206Z; rate: admin at 09:12:20.171Z and root at 09:12:20.319Z - after which every 'Authentication succeeded' entry comes from the application pod addresses (geo 10.244.7.237, rate 10.244.125.39); no later localhost admin authentication appears in that window.

The rate path is served entirely from cache and the geo path performs no measurable DB work: over the hour to 09:14:17Z the profile span 'mongo_profile' and the rate span 'mongo_rate' both have count 0 (all GetRates/GetProfiles work is memcached_get_multi_rate / memcached_get_profile), the geo server span averages 0.080 ms, and mongodb-geo received only 24.4 B/s while mongodb-rate received 61.1 B/s and mongodb-reservation received 836.7 B/s in the last 2 minutes.

The rate service's own counters show no shedding or failure: rate_requests_received_total 4453 = rate_requests_completed_total 4453, rate_requests_rejected_total 0, rate_requests_expired_total 0, rate_in_flight 0, rate_queue_depth 0 (queue_capacity 256, backend_qps_limit 500), and the search-side counters search_rate_attempts_total 4170 = search_rate_successes_total 4170 with search_rate_failures_total 0 and search_rate_timeouts_total 0 (i.e. no retry or timeout occurred).

The per-service blackbox probes of the application endpoints succeed after startup: probe_success=1 at 09:13:17-09:14:17Z for frontend.hotel-reservation:5000, geo:8083, profile:8081, rate:8084, recommendation:8085, reservation:8087, search:8082 and user:8086 (they were 0 at 09:12:17-09:12:47Z while the pods were still starting, with probe_duration ~1.5-4.4 ms).

probe_success for instance 'http://ingress-nginx-controller.ingress-nginx/api/hotels?inDate=2015-04-09&outDate=2015-04-10&lat=38.0235&lon=-122.095' (job blackbox-ingress-hotel-reservation) is 0 with probe_http_status_code 0 at every sample 09:12:17-09:14:17Z, but this does not indicate an application fault: the cluster currently holds 0 Ingress objects and namespace ingress-nginx has 0 deployments (no ingress-nginx-controller), so the probe targets a controller that does not exist.

Connection-refused-by-policy and quota-exhaustion are ruled out as mechanisms: there are no NetworkPolicy objects and no ResourceQuota objects in the cluster, and all four nodes (sregym-control-plane, sregym-worker, sregym-worker2, sregym-worker3) are Ready=True with MemoryPressure/DiskPressure/PIDPressure=False.

Rejected for the observed window: that the incident is the prepared MongoDB privilege revocation on geo-db or rate-db. The revoke scripts exist and are mounted in both mongo pods, but no localhost admin authentication to mongodb-geo or mongodb-rate occurred after the 09:12:20-09:12:21Z init run inside 09:12:00-09:14:17Z (the script authenticates as admin against 127.0.0.1), and no failure signal appears on either path: rate handled 4453/4453 requests with 0 rejected/expired, search made 4170 rate calls with 0 failures and 0 timeouts, and no application error or 5xx appeared.

Rejected: that reservation-application latency/errors are caused by CPU throttling or by pods not starting normally. Throttled-CFS-period ratio is 0 for every hotel-reservation pod, no container restart occurred (restartCount 0 on all 21 pods), and the only non-ready conditions in the namespace belong to the audit-log-archiver CronJob pods, not to any of the 19 application pods.

The firing KubePodNotReady alert is explained by the CronJob pod template rather than by an application fault: because 'archiver' exits (correctly, exit 0) while 'fluent-bit-sidecar' runs forever and no readinessProbe exists, the pod can never be Ready and the Job can never complete; consequently the CronJob re-creates a Job every minute (29925193, 29925194, 29925195 observed), accumulating permanently non-Ready pods. The archiver's own archive/forward step succeeded, so no reservation-path impact is expected from this.

A geo-db or rate-db MongoDB privilege fault could be present yet invisible here: geo answers /geo.Geo/Nearby in about 62-80 us with essentially no mongo traffic (mongodb-geo ~24 B/s) and rate serves 100% of GetRates from memcached (mongo_rate span count 0), so neither service would surface a revoked 'admin' readWrite role until it needed the database again; this remains unverified rather than excluded.

Advice: change the audit-log-archiver CronJob pod template so the archiver pod can complete - either drop the perpetual fluent-bit-sidecar from the Job pod, or run the sidecar in a long-lived Deployment/Service instead of inside the Job pod (optionally add an activeDeadlineSeconds/ttlSecondsAfterFinished) - so completed archives stop producing permanently non-Ready pods and a new stuck Job every minute.

Advice: verify MongoDB privileges directly before any further conclusion - for example db.getUser('admin') and db.getRoles on geo-db and rate-db in mongodb-geo and mongodb-rate, or a forced cache-miss read on rate-db and a geo-db query - because credentials live in Secrets that cannot be read in this run, and neither path exercises Mongo during ordinary request handling.

Advice: capture a longer steady-state baseline before judging any latency or throughput regression - the deployment that owns the observed pods begins at 2026-11-24T09:12:11Z (mongo ReplicaSets 09:12:11Z-09:12:16Z, workflow events from 09:10:25Z), so no pre-incident comparison exists inside this window.

gaps: No samples exist before the environment was created (app pods start 09:12:11Z, monitoring stack events from 09:10:25Z), so there is no pre-incident baseline for latency, request rate or error rate; all statements here rest on roughly 09:12:11-09:15:00Z.

gRPC-level error codes are not observable: the only status_code value present on traces_span_metrics_calls_total is STATUS_CODE_UNSET for every service and there is no rpc_grpc_status_code series (queries for rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count returned nothing), so error spans that the application never marked cannot be counted.

MongoDB user roles/privileges could not be verified directly - credentials are in Secrets that cannot be read - so whether user 'admin' currently holds readWrite on geo-db or rate-db is unknown; the negative result about the revoke scripts covers only localhost authentications visible in mongodb-geo/mongodb-rate logs for 09:12:00-09:14:17Z.

MongoDB command-level logs were not available to confirm or refute authorization failures: mongodb-geo logged only one line after 09:13:00Z (a WiredTiger checkpoint) and no error/authorization entries were found.

The wrk2 load-generator log is internally inconsistent and was therefore not used as evidence: it reports 'Socket errors: ... timeout 187/188/189' per 30 s round against ~2934-2972 requests while the recorded latency maximum is 6.61-9.20 ms and no 'Non-2xx or 3xx responses' line was found; the cause of those timeouts is unknown, and the wrk2 pod no longer exists so its Job spec and target path could not be inspected.
Absence of error lines in logs and of error statuses in traces is not proof of absence: log retention, the Loki line limit and the projection/sampling of traces could hide events I did not see.

The change_history integration is not available in this Run, so what changed (if anything) before the environment came up at 09:10-09:12Z cannot be reconstructed; deployment managedFields only record the last write time (kubectl-patch at 09:12:12Z on mongodb-geo/mongodb-rate) and not which fields changed.

The alert or prompt that triggered this Run is not stated in the delivered context, so the intended incident is unknown; the only firing signal at window end was KubePodNotReady on the audit-log-archiver pods.

hypothesis.text: The firing KubePodNotReady alert is explained by the CronJob pod template rather than by an application fault: because 'archiver' exits (correctly, exit 0) while 'fluent-bit-sidecar' runs forever and no readinessProbe exists, the pod can never be Ready and the Job can never complete; consequently the CronJob re-creates a Job every minute (29925193, 29925194, 29925195 observed), accumulating permanently non-Ready pods. The archiver's own archive/forward step succeeded, so no reservation-path impact is expected from this.

A geo-db or rate-db MongoDB privilege fault could be present yet invisible here: geo answers /geo.Geo/Nearby in about 62-80 us with essentially no mongo traffic (mongodb-geo ~24 B/s) and rate serves 100% of GetRates from memcached (mongo_rate span count 0), so neither service would surface a revoked 'admin' readWrite role until it needed the database again; this remains unverified rather than excluded.

Advice: verify MongoDB privileges directly before any further conclusion - for example db.getUser('admin') and db.getRoles on geo-db and rate-db in mongodb-geo and mongodb-rate, or a forced cache-miss read on rate-db and a geo-db query - because credentials live in Secrets that cannot be read in this run, and neither path exercises Mongo during ordinary request handling.

#!/bin/bash


ROOT_USER="root"
ROOT_PWD="root"

echo "Removing admin user..."

mongo admin -u $ROOT_USER -p $ROOT_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \

data.revoke-admin-geo-mongo.sh:
#!/bin/bash


ADMIN_USER="admin"
ADMIN_PWD="admin"
# TARGET_DB="rate-db"
TARGET_DB="geo-db"

echo "Downgrading admin user privileges..."

# Connect to MongoDB and revoke roles
mongo admin -u $ADMIN_USER -p $ADMIN_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.revokeRolesFromUser('$ADMIN_USER', [{role: 'readWrite', db: '$TARGET_DB'}]);"

echo "Privileges downgraded"
data.remove-mitigate-admin-geo-mongo.sh:
#!/bin/bash


ROOT_USER="root"
ROOT_PWD="root"

ADMIN_USER="admin"
ADMIN_PWD="admin"
READ_WRITE_ROLE="readWrite"
TARGET_DB="geo-db"

echo "Recreating admin user..."

# Connect to MongoDB and create the admin user
mongo admin -u $ROOT_USER -p $ROOT_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.createUser({user: '$ADMIN_USER', pwd: '$ADMIN_PWD', roles:[{role:'userAdminAnyDatabase',db:'admin'}]});"

echo "Admin user recreated"

# Grant readWrite role on the target database
echo "Granting readWrite role to $ADMIN_USER on $TARGET_DB database..."
mongo admin -u $ROOT_USER -p $ROOT_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.grantRolesToUser('$ADMIN_USER', [{role: '$READ_WRITE_ROLE', db: '$TARGET_DB'}]);"

echo "Privileges restored successfully"
